_about: Finisher templates as data (Combat). A finisher replaces the rest of a decisive exchange when the loser is on the brink (spec-wounds.md section 1; exchange.gd startFinisher). Roles are W (the winner, who performs it) and L (the loser on the brink); the loader maps them to 'A'/'D' exactly as startFinisher does. Beat times are relative to the finisher's start (t0 = ex.t when startFinisher runs). 'generic.placeholder' reproduces today's placeholder set piece bit for bit (profile 'parity'); the authored finishers use integer ticks (60 per second). Contract and verification: docs/combat/data-fields.md section 10 and docs/combat/s3b-loader-note.md.

select._rule: parity profile: always 'generic.placeholder'. authored profile: the winner's own finisher by fighter name (e.g. 'KAI'), else 'generic'. Later: by fighter and form tier (damage-model.md section 5).

contest._timeCapAt: seconds (11:00): the director's stand-in for the time-cap event. From then on every decisive win against a fighter on the brink is a finisher, with no set-up needed. 0 or absent is off. The full event (both on the brink, no Rallies, the 60 s winner rule) is Game Design's and Simulation's
contest._brinkSetups: the brink chapter (spec-wounds.md section 1b): decisive wins the rival needs against a fighter on the brink before it is open to a finisher. The exchange that causes the brink is never one. Game Design: 2 if brink to KO stays under a 45 s median
contest._note: survival chance = max(floor, base - tiltPerMinute * max(0, (T - tiltAfter) / 60)) - rallyPenalty per Rally used (Rally is S4; the parity profile ignores rallyPenalty). One S.rng.next() when the contest resolves: survived if draw < chance. Numbers are Game Design's (spec-wounds.md section 1); constants match exchange.gd lines 261-263.

scoring.tilts: the contest's rallyPenalty per Rally used and tiltPerMinute past tiltAfter, as above

byState.fighterState: hooks keyed by roster data: Protagonist Simmering or Boiling +0.10, Anti-hero Pride 50+ +0.10, Empress any guard standing +0.05, Cyborg hatch closed +0.10
byState.pulses: at beatTicks (18, 36, 54): struggle_pulse holding or slipping, revealing the drawn result with no further draw
byState._note: spec-wounds.md section 1: the struggle is resolved by state and drawn once at contestOpen. The stance names are the sim's; under ADR 0008 they are the held states Guard, Dodge and Press. The press fields above (halfWidthTicks, assistHalfWidthTicks, debounceTicks, inputs, aiHitChance) and the press scoring retire when Encounter switches the struggle to this block

struggle._note: Used by the authored profile. Ticks are counted from contestOpen, which sits 66 ticks before contest in every authored finisher; the cue just before contestOpen (final_windup, ascend_charge, lift_and_display) is the count-in. Widths and rhythm: Controls (rulings section 8). Scoring: Game Design (spec-wounds.md section 1). aiHitChance: Encounter maps difficulty to it (0.44 to 0.78 fits QA's 20 to 35% survival band). The contest still draws once, so the RNG sequence does not depend on the number of presses. Parity ignores this block (base 0.30, no input).

cues._about: render-only cue vocabulary used by the 'cue' op here and in templates.json. The simulation only emits the event (no state change, no RNG). Looks are for VFX, Camera, Audio and UI.
cues.finisher_open: freeze-frame and zoom on the winner; the FINISHER banner; the start of a short set-piece pause (Orb: short pauses at set pieces)
cues.catch: the winner halts or seizes the flying loser
cues.ascend_charge: the winner rises above the loser, charging; wide upward framing
cues.lift_and_display: the winner hoists the loser and turns toward the nearest settlement; a bark
cues._bark: a cue's bark arg is a line-system trigger id (finisher_landed, finisher_survived), or true for a bark pause with no trigger assigned yet
cues.struggle: the contest window: the loser's last-ditch struggle, with the survival chance on the HUD
cues.last_look: camera push-in and a bark pause before the final blow
cues.breaks_hold: the loser bursts free: aura flare, afterimage
cues.holds_on: the loser, battered, squares up again; HOLDS ON banner
cues.tell: a readable warning pose on the named fighter
cues.whiff_recover: the attacker's swing cuts empty air
cues.turn_read: the attacker pivots, reading the dodge
cues.exposed: the attacker is caught off balance
cues.recover: the named fighter recovers its stance
cues.guard_set: the guard holds and shoves back
cues.bind: forearms lock for a beat before the deciding blow
cues.backstep: the attacker gives ground before lunging back in for the deciding blow (same side, no pass-through)
cues.perfect_block: a perfect block: a sharp deflect flash on the guard, the attacker staggers
cues.riposte: the riposte after a perfect block: an unblockable answer
cues.reversal: a guard-cancel turn into the defender's own attack
cues.tell_light: the attacker's light-weight tell through the approach (driven by the attack event's kind)
cues.tell_heavy: the attacker's heavy-weight tell through the approach: a coil, a glowing fist
cues.finisher_tell_launch: the finisher's wind-up shows a launch finisher (read: Guard)
cues.finisher_tell_melee: the finisher's wind-up shows a melee finisher (read: Dodge)
cues.finisher_tell_beam: the finisher's wind-up shows a beam finisher (read: answer with a beam)
cues.blink_meet: a mid-air meet: fist and forearm spark
cues.chain_ender: the chain's full stop: heavier flash, CHAIN xN
cues.blitz: a fast chain: speed lines, rhythm accent
cues.relay: aerial chain: overtake and strike back
cues.volley_fire: small energy bolts leave the hand
cues.clash_seesaw: beam push swings back and forth
cues.clash_split: beams bend apart and carve twin trenches
cues.clash_deflect: one beam angles the other away
cues.circle: the attacker swings around to the far side before the deciding blow
cues.recoil: both fighters thrown back by the clash

shapes._about: Shapes for the four real fighters' finishers, to be authored when their parts and forms exist. Each is a skeleton with fixed slots (what makes it that fighter's finisher) and generative slots (filled by the procedural composer, procedural-moves.md sections 4.2 and 7). Every one keeps the same contest and the same two outcomes. Budget: 3 to 8 s to the final blow (section 10 set pieces). Variants by form tier are expected (damage-model.md section 5). Names are Narrative's, screened by Legal.
